cards.title: Fifteen minutes with the doctor goes fast
cards.body: Then you're in the auto home remembering everything you forgot to ask. A few notes beforehand make the visit count.

cards.title: Every medicine they actually take
cards.body: Not just what's on the last prescription. Include ones from other doctors, anything the chemist suggested and any home remedies. Carrying the strips works too.

cards.title: What's changed since last time
cards.body: New symptoms, when they started, how often. "Dizzy in the mornings, three times this week" helps far more than "tabiyat theek nahi hai".

cards.title: Home readings, if you take them
cards.body: BP or sugar readings with date and time. A photo of the notebook works. Patterns tell the doctor more than one scary number.

cards.title: Missed doses and side effects
cards.body: Be honest about skipped tablets or ones that cause trouble. Doctors can only adjust what they know about.

cards.title: Your top three questions
cards.body: Write them down and ask them first. Anything else is a bonus. Note the answers before you leave the room.

cards.title: Walk in with one page
cards.body: Medicines, changes, readings, questions. One page, and the doctor gets the real picture instead of half of it.

takeaway: Before a doctor visit, list all medicines, recent changes, home readings, missed doses and your top three questions.
share: Send this to whoever is taking Papa for his check-up this week.
